function: Over-the-air aggregation of local models in decentralized federated learning: joint design of transceiver beamformers and mixing matrix over MIMO full-duplex D2D links (p. 2, p. 7).
system: Ad hoc D2D network of M=30 devices, each with NT=NR=20 antennas by default, in-band full-duplex, block fading; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 4, p. 9).
method: Alternating optimization (convex QCQP and closed form for beamformers, convex program for mixing matrix); CNN trained by decentralized SGD, federated, supervised (p. 7, p. 8).
data_channel: Own i.i.d. Rayleigh fading simulator; MNIST (20k training, 10k validation samples) with a heterogeneous split over 30 devices; no standard channel model or measurement (p. 8, p. 9).
test_conditions: Training and testing share the Rayleigh model and MNIST task; results versus antennas, SNR, devices, topology sparsity; no unseen-condition test; 30 trials (p. 9, p. 10).
baselines: Joint optimization with separate OTA aggregation [39]; digital communication [40], zero-forcing [28], and MMSE beamforming [18], each with random mixing matrix; error-free case; centralized FL (p. 9, 11, 12).
metrics: Minimum and average test accuracy across devices, and communication NMSE in dB (p. 9, p. 10).
complexity: Worst-case order O(Jmax(I1max M N^3.5 + I2max M^7)) for Algorithm 2, N = NT; CNN has 21880 parameters; no runtime reported (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 9: "We model the communication channels as independently and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh fading"; custom simulator, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or COST 2100 model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "we initially investigate the impact of the number of transmitter and receiver antennas"; only sweeps over antennas, SNR, devices and sparsity; no model tested in an unseen scenario, no fine-tuning or transfer.
q3_support: p. 11: "Joint optimization with separate over-the-air aggregation (JO with SOA) [39]" and "Zero-forcing beamforming without mixing matrix optimization (ZFB w/o MMO) [28]"; p. 12: "the proposed algorithm achieves nearly the same accuracy as the JO with SOA scheme".
q4_support: p. 8: "worst-case complexity of Algorithm 2 can be expressed as O(Jmax (I1max M N 3.5 +I2max M 7 ))".
q5_support: p. 8: "We perform the learning task of image classification on the MNIST dataset [36]"; MNIST is a learning-task dataset, channels are simulated (p. 9), and no code or data link is given.
notes: Included under the federated-learning-over-the-air rule: the proposed design is convex alternating optimization, but the learned element is the CNN trained across devices (p. 8). Area 7, since the problem solved is the over-the-air aggregation itself (p. 2). q3 marked met on the reading that [39], [28], [40], [18] are earlier published aggregation designs; the paper adapts them (random mixing matrix, time-division version of [39], p. 11-12), so the reviewer should confirm. q4 counts the complexity of the aggregation and transceiver design.
